A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VIGS-SLAM and contain readable main text and supplementary material. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison across the substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original VIGS-SLAM tracking, rendering, robustness, ablation and runtime results in the main paper and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds self-captured-dataset evaluations, baseline comparisons, visual-corruption experiments, additional ablations and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions retain joint pose/disparity/velocity/bias optimization, three-stage IMU initialization, IMU-based keyframe initialization, pose-graph loop closure and consistent Gaussian updates. v2 adds solver and sampling details and reports implementation acceleration; these do not establish a different estimator, objective or core algorithm.

E1.justification: The four original benchmarks remain. Self-captured evaluation expands from one extreme-condition sequence to 18 indoor/outdoor sequences covering long trajectories, dynamic objects, glare, low light and reflective/transparent surfaces. Controlled motion-blur, overexposure and low-light variants of EuRoC introduce additional input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds DBA-Fusion and VINGS-Mono to tracking comparisons on the original benchmarks, increasing the stated baseline set from 13 to 15. VINGS-Mono also enters rendering comparisons, including Table 3 and Figure 3. It was discussed but not evaluated in v1; these additions directly address closely related visual-inertial competitors.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled blur, exposure and noisy low-light transformations, success-curve AUC through 6 meters, and peak GPU-memory measurement. Newly evaluated baselines use specified adaptations: forced EuRoC keyframes, a reduced UTMM initialization threshold, and disabled monocular depth and loop closure for VINGS-Mono. The original ATE, recall and rendering metrics remain.

E4.justification: Table 6 expands from three tracking ablations to six, adding zero-bias, shared-global-bias and removal-of-inertial-only-initialization tests. v2 also adds controlled corruption sensitivity tests and broader trajectory/rendering case studies. Conversely, v1's appendix Tables 17–18 with per-sequence mapping and tracking ablations disappear, although their aggregate results remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's synthetic-noise parameters describe input corruption, not uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: Original benchmark accuracy/rendering results are largely retained, but v2 adds extensive baseline, self-capture, corruption and ablation results. Table 10 reports self-captured mean ATE of 0.588 m for VIGS-SLAM versus 1.850 m for DBA-Fusion. Runtime Table 9 changes mean tracking/full-system FPS from 16.40/7.09 to 39.83/12.02, while mean keyframes change from 491 to 366; this is not an isolated same-workload speedup. Some per-sequence ablation results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds the block normal equations and Schur-complement update in Section 3.1, Equation 4, including the argument that the depth block is diagonal. v1 states the residual objectives without this algebra. Other core mathematical formulations remain equivalent, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: tightly coupled visual-inertial estimation, robust initialization, time-varying biases, consistent loop-closure updates, robust real-time tracking and high-fidelity mapping. Expanding evaluation from four named benchmarks to five datasets supplies broader support rather than redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific explanations involving DBA-Fusion's linearization gap and VINGS-Mono's depth generalization and loop-closure failures. Its limitations paragraph replaces the multicamera/fisheye and high-end-GPU caveats with marginal gains from Gaussian-assisted pose refinement, attributed to insufficiently sharp online renderings. These refine mechanisms and applicability discussion without overturning the main interpretation.

D1.justification: v1 describes partially NumPy-based IMU processing and future CUDA optimization; v2 reports C++ preintegration, CUDA Jacobian/Hessian computation and TensorRT inference. It also adds baseline configuration details, smartphone-demo implementation, and Odin acquisition, calibration, undistortion and anonymization information. The project-page link is replaced by promises to release code and data, which do not establish current availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around newly cited DBA-Fusion, acknowledging its earlier use of DROID-SLAM correspondences and contrasting its cascaded optimization with VIGS-SLAM's coupled solve. The existing VINGS-Mono discussion is recast around that relationship and specific weaknesses. Additional references support implementation and acquisition; KITTI and KITTI-360 citations are removed.

P1.justification: The main section order and much existing prose remain. v2 makes targeted introductory and related-work rewrites, expands optimization and ablation explanations, updates author/front matter, and adds dedicated supplementary sections for the demo and baselines. References move behind the supplementary narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Figure 2 is reorganized; Figure 3 adds VINGS-Mono and replaces the HKU example with Retail. New self-capture Figures 5–6 replace the earlier single-case display. Tables gain comparator, ablation and memory rows, new experimental tables appear, and two detailed appendix ablation tables are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1: missing empirical comparisons with closely related dense visual-inertial systems and limited tests of staged initialization and bias modeling. The added comparisons, targeted ablations, controlled corruptions and diverse self-captured sequences substantially strengthen support for robustness. Implementation documentation also improves. Removed per-sequence ablation tables and less explicit hardware/camera caveats reduce transparency, while changed keyframe counts limit runtime comparability, but these losses do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
